events.title: Laban kisses his family and returns home
events.narrative_summary: Early in the morning Laban kisses his sons and daughters, blesses them and goes back to his place.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'Laban rose early in the morning' (32:1): the morning after the covenant night (evt.gen_31.covenant_feast, which stayed the night). Anchored on its END with BOKER; the farewell takes about an hour.

events.title: Angels of God meet Jacob and he names Mahanaim
events.narrative_summary: Jacob goes on his way and angels of God meet him. Seeing them he says 'This is God's camp' and calls the place Mahanaim.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No time word. Jacob leaves the Gilead hill country after Laban and reaches Mahanaim, a day or so of travel with flocks and children (Onkelos and Pseudo-Jonathan add nothing on timing); offset 1 day, margin 1 day, from Laban's departure END.

events.title: Jacob sends messengers to Esau in Edom
events.narrative_summary: Jacob sends messengers ahead to his brother Esau in the land of Seir, the country of Edom, with words of submission and a report of his wealth, seeking favour.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows the naming of Mahanaim directly; no delay stated. Starts at the END of the angels event, margin 1 day; the instructions take about an hour.

events.title: Messengers report Esau is coming with 400 men
events.narrative_summary: The messengers return to Jacob and say that Esau is coming to meet him with four hundred men.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No duration in the text. urim travel Mahanaim to Edom, 'hurry': about 200 km by road, 40 h moving, ~4 days each way. Esau is already marching toward Jacob (32:7), so the round trip is shorter than 8 days: offset 6 days, margin 3 days.

events.title: Jacob, afraid, divides his people into two camps
events.narrative_summary: Jacob is greatly afraid and distressed. He divides his people, flocks, herds and camels into two camps, reasoning that if Esau strikes one the other may escape.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Immediate reaction to the report (32:8), so it starts at the END of the report with no delay; dividing a household and herds takes about 3 hours.

events.title: Jacob prays to be delivered from Esau
events.narrative_summary: Jacob prays to the God of Abraham and Isaac, confesses he is unworthy of God's kindness, asks to be saved from Esau, and recalls God's promise of good and countless descendants.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: The prayer follows the division of the camps (his words 'I have become two camps', 32:11); no delay is stated, so it starts at the END of the division. A short prayer, about 20 minutes.

events.title: Jacob lodges and selects a gift for Esau
events.narrative_summary: Jacob lodges there that night and takes from what he has a gift for Esau: goats, sheep, camels, cattle and donkeys.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'He lodged there that night' (32:14): evening after the prayer, so EREV from the END of the prayer (the prayer ends mid-afternoon in the chain, so the evening is the same day); the selection takes about 2 hours.

events.title: Jacob sends the gift in droves with instructions
events.narrative_summary: Jacob gives each drove to a servant, tells them to go ahead with a space between droves, and tells each what to say if Esau asks whose they are: a gift from Jacob, who is behind them.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Continuous with the choosing of the gift on the same evening; starts at its END, about 2 hours to divide the droves and give the instructions.

events.title: The gift crosses ahead while Jacob stays in the camp
events.narrative_summary: The gift goes on ahead of Jacob, and he spends that night in the camp.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: The execution of the preceding instructions the same evening (32:22 'that night'); starts at their END, about half an hour to set off.

events.title: Jacob rises by night and sends his family over the Jabbok
events.narrative_summary: That night Jacob gets up, takes his two wives, two maids and eleven sons across the ford of the Jabbok, and sends over all he has.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'He rose in that night' (32:23). Radak: after a little sleep. Offset 90 minutes after the gift left puts the start near midnight; margin 2 hours; crossing a household and herds about 2 hours (stay in camp is in 32:22).

events.title: A man wrestles with Jacob until dawn and wrenches his hip
events.narrative_summary: Jacob is left alone and a man wrestles with him until dawn. Seeing he cannot prevail, the man touches the socket of Jacob's thigh and it is put out of joint.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'Until the coming up of the dawn' (32:25; Ibn Ezra: the end of night's darkness, or the glow before sunrise). Starts when the crossing ends (about 02:00) and runs 3 hours; the dawn scene follows at SHACHAR. Pseudo-Jonathan's expansion (the angel speaking of tithes) is not used.
events.ancient_diurnal_marker: Until the breaking of the day

events.title: Jacob demands a blessing and is renamed Israel
events.narrative_summary: The man asks to be let go because the dawn has come, but Jacob will not release him until he blesses him. He asks Jacob's name, renames him Israel for striving with God and men and prevailing, refuses to give his own name, and blesses him there.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'Let me go, for the dawn has come up' (32:27) fixes it at first light: SHACHAR after the wrestling, DIURNAL_HOUR. The exchange takes about 20 minutes.
events.ancient_diurnal_marker: For the dawn has come up

events.title: Jacob names the place Peniel
events.narrative_summary: Jacob calls the place Peniel, saying he has seen God face to face and his life is preserved.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Immediately after the blessing (32:31), no delay; a moment's action of 5 minutes, same dawn scene.

events.title: The sun rises on Jacob limping past Penuel
events.narrative_summary: As Jacob passes Penuel the sun rises on him and he limps because of his thigh.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'The sun rose upon him as he passed Penuel' (32:32): sunrise, BOKER, snapped after the naming; lasts about an hour while he moves on.

causal_edges.causal_explanation: Having been blessed and having seen God face to face, Jacob names the place Peniel (32:31).
Hearing that Esau comes with 400 men, Jacob is afraid and divides his camp (32:8).
Fear of Esau's approach leads Jacob to prepare a gift to appease him (32:14, 32:21).
Jacob's messengers go to Esau and come back with his answer (32:7).
Jacob's commands to the servants are carried out as the gift goes on ahead (32:22).
Because Jacob held on and would not let the man go without a blessing, he receives the name Israel (32:27-29).
The dislocated thigh socket makes Jacob limp as the sun rises (32:26, 32:32).

entities.etymology_meaning: Hebrew 'minkha', a gift or tribute offered to a superior.
entities.summary_bio: Jacob selects 550 animals from his herds as a gift to appease Esau: goats, sheep, camels, cattle and donkeys, in separate droves with a space between them.
The company of 400 men that, according to Jacob's messengers, accompanies Esau as he comes to meet Jacob. Their purpose is not stated, and Jacob fears the worst.

entities.etymology_meaning: Hebrew 'mal'akhim' means 'messengers'; the same word is used for the angels of God in 32:2.
entities.summary_bio: Messengers Jacob sends to Esau in Seir with a placating message. They return with the news that Esau is coming with 400 men.
The male and female servants of Jacob's household. Some are given the droves of the gift for Esau and told what to say to him.

entities.etymology_meaning: 'Red', from the red stew Esau ate and his ruddy appearance (Gen 25:30).
entities.summary_bio: The region southeast of Canaan associated with Esau, called 'the field of Edom' in the land of Seir. Jacob sends his messengers there to Esau.

entities.etymology_meaning: Probably related to a root meaning 'to empty out' or 'to wrestle', a likely wordplay with 'he wrestled' (vayye'avek).
entities.summary_bio: A river east of the Jordan flowing into it from the east. Jacob sends his family and possessions across its ford by night before his wrestling at the crossing.

entities.etymology_meaning: Dual form of 'camp': 'two camps', probably after the camp of God's angels and Jacob's own camp.
entities.summary_bio: A place east of the Jordan, in Gilead, where angels of God meet Jacob as he returns from Haran. Jacob names it Mahanaim, and he sends messengers to Esau from here.

entities.etymology_meaning: 'Face of God', from Jacob's words 'I have seen God face to face'.
entities.summary_bio: A place by the Jabbok where Jacob wrestles with a man until dawn and is renamed Israel. Jacob names it Peniel and passes on from it limping at sunrise.

entities.canonical_name: The man who wrestled with Jacob
entities.etymology_meaning: Hebrew 'ish', simply 'a man'; he refuses to give his name.
entities.summary_bio: An unnamed 'man' who wrestles with Jacob at night by the Jabbok. He wrenches Jacob's hip, renames him Israel and blesses him; Jacob concludes he has seen God face to face. The text does not name him, and later tradition (Hosea 12) speaks of an angel.

components.evidence_explanation: GEN.32.14: Jacob takes the gift for Esau from what he has with him.
GEN.32.8: 'Jacob was greatly afraid and distressed' when he hears that Esau is coming with 400 men.
GEN.32.26: the man touches the socket of Jacob's thigh and it is dislocated; 32.32 shows him limping.
GEN.32.29: 'Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel.'
GEN.32.3: Jacob names the place Mahanaim after the angels meet him, and sends messengers from there.
GEN.32.25–32.31: Jacob remains alone at the Jabbok, wrestles, and names the place Peniel.

systems.name: Gift to appease an offended party
systems.ancient_near_east_context: Gifts (minkha) were offered to superiors or offended parties to secure favour, as with tribute and diplomatic gifts. Hebrew uses the verb 'to cover the face' (kipper) for placating anger by gift.
rules_and_mechanics: The gift is sent ahead of the giver so that it reaches the recipient first.
It is presented as belonging to the giver ('your servant Jacob's').
The giver hopes the recipient will 'lift up his face', that is, receive him favourably.

systems.name: Wrestling with a divine being
systems.ancient_near_east_context: Physical contests between a mortal and a god or divine messenger are told in other traditions as well, and the Hebrew Bible looks back on this one in Hosea 12:3–5. Here the text itself ties the contest to a night at the Jabbok crossing, a blessing and a change of name; whether that pattern recurs is not attested in the text.
rules_and_mechanics: The contest runs from night until the dawn rises (32:25).
The being cannot prevail over the mortal, and strikes his thigh socket so that it is dislocated (32:26).
The being declares that the mortal has struggled with God and with men and has prevailed (32:29).
The mortal refuses to release the being until he is blessed (32:27), and receives a new name and a blessing (32:28–30).
The mortal is left limping at sunrise (32:32).

systems.name: Sending an embassy of messengers
systems.ancient_near_east_context: In the ancient Near East parties in conflict or distance exchanged messengers who recited a message in the sender's voice, as seen in the Mari and Amarna letters. The messenger formula 'thus says your servant' also appears in diplomatic letters.
rules_and_mechanics: The sender instructs the messengers on the exact words to say.
The message uses deferential titles ('my lord', 'your servant').
Messengers return with a report of the recipient's response or movements.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Angels of God meet Jacob on his way, and he recognises them as God's camp.
system_instances.significance_note: Marks God's protection at the threshold of the land and prepares for the fear of meeting Esau.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Messengers go to Esau in Seir with Jacob's deferential greeting, calling Esau 'my lord' and Jacob 'your servant'.
system_instances.significance_note: The first approach to Esau after twenty years; the messengers return with the news that Esau comes with 400 men.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Jacob sends droves of animals in succession, each led by a servant who says the animals are Jacob's gift to 'my lord Esau'.
system_instances.significance_note: Jacob aims to 'cover Esau's face' with the gift before meeting him and hopes Esau will receive him.

system_instances.outcome_summary: The man asks Jacob's name and renames him Israel, because he has struggled with God and men and prevailed.
system_instances.significance_note: Gives Jacob the name of the nation and marks the end of 'the supplanter'.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Jacob names the place Mahanaim, 'two camps'.
system_instances.significance_note: The name recalls God's camp, and echoes Jacob's own two camps in 32:8, 32:11.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Jacob names the place Peniel, 'face of God', because he has seen God face to face and lived.
system_instances.significance_note: Interprets the night as an encounter with God and sets up the face-to-face meeting with Esau in GEN.33.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Jacob asks God to deliver him and his family from Esau, recalling God's promises of return and of descendants.
system_instances.significance_note: Jacob's first recorded prayer; he confesses his unworthiness and claims the promise.

system_instances.outcome_summary: A man wrestles with Jacob until dawn and, unable to prevail, wrenches Jacob's hip.
system_instances.significance_note: The turning point of Jacob's life: he is left alone, wounded and blessed before meeting Esau.

edges.description: Angels of God meet Jacob on his way.
Jacob plans to cover Esau's face with the gift sent before him.
Jacob tells his messengers exactly what to say to Esau.
Jacob gives his servants the droves and tells them what to say to Esau.
Jacob refuses to let the man go unless he blesses him.
Jacob is terrified when he hears that Esau is coming with 400 men.
Jacob prays to the God of Abraham and Isaac to deliver him from Esau.
Jacob sends messengers ahead to his brother Esau in Seir.
Laban kisses and blesses his daughter Leah before returning home.
Laban kisses and blesses his daughter Rachel before returning home.
The man declines to give his name and blesses Jacob there.
The man says Jacob's name will be Israel, because he has struggled with God and men and prevailed.
Unable to prevail, the man touches Jacob's hip socket and dislocates it.
A man wrestles with Jacob at night until dawn.
